clue.text: Leader to swallow insult: take time off to dye

indicators.note: the leader to a word is its opening letter, here of the word swallow
take, paired with off later, says a letter is removed from the insult
off completes take ... off, telling us to drop the time letter

parts.note: to affront someone is to insult them; as a noun an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: A leader is told to put up with an insult and take time off to dye something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader to swallow' reads as an order given to a leader, but 'Leader to' picks the first letter of the next word; 'take ... off' straddles 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a yellow-orange colouring obtained from crocus stigmas, used as a dye.

clue.text: Got rid of surrounding pole, cut short

indicators.note: surrounding means the phrase for got rid of goes around the pole letter

parts.note: saw off is the past of see off, to get rid of
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Someone removed the fencing around a pole that was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the phrasal verb round the pole. A sawn-off shotgun has its barrel cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn-off describes something shortened by sawing, especially a shotgun barrel.

clue.text: More light, say, for old madrigals about tailless beast on two roads

indicators.note: about means the song refrains go around the shortened beast

parts.note: fa-las are the nonsense refrains of old madrigals, and so the songs themselves

indicators.note: tailless means the creature loses its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a small beast
RD is the standard abbreviation for road, so roads gives RDS

explanation.surface: Asking for more light, an old singer of madrigals tells of a beast on two roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More light' is traditionally Goethe's dying utterance, and 'say' marks it as an example; 'tailless' and 'about' work on the beast and the song refrains.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe's dying cry 'More light!' is a classic example of a person's last utterance.

clue.text: Anger directed against European surveyor's mark

indicators.note: directed suggests the letters are steered into a new order

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Anger aimed at a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directed' rearranges ANGER into RANGE; 'against' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A range pole is a striped rod a surveyor sets up to mark a line or point.

clue.text: Sound of organ having setter at the heart

indicators.note: at the heart means the setter's letter sits in the middle of the organ

parts.note: the nose is an organ of the body
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: An organ's sound comes from the composer at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself, giving I. 'Sound' looks like 'sound of organ' music, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Be happy! Have a cigarette!

definitions.meaning: a face lights up when its owner becomes cheerful
to light a cigarette is to ...

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to brighten with joy and to ignite a cigarette and start smoking.

clue.text: Parisian dance to endure: sunburn to disappear

parts.note: to last is to endure
a tan is skin darkened by the sun
to go is to disappear

explanation.surface: A dance in Paris must endure until the sunburn fades.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the film 'Last Tango in Paris'.
explanation.definitionFit: The film 'Last Tango in Paris' gives this tango its Parisian setting.

clue.text: Speaker's forbidding writers of tales

indicators.note: a speaker's word is one said out loud, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding

explanation.surface: A speaker refuses to let writers of tales speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forbidding' looks like a verb, but here it is an adjective meaning stern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm wrote down the famous collection of German fairy tales.

clue.text: Miniature digit with hard objects on boat

parts.note: a thumb is a digit of the hand
nails are small hard objects
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A small finger with sharp things on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a brief small-scale drawing or description, a miniature.

clue.text: Parson in confined stop

indicators.note: in means the clergyman is placed inside the word for confined

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined
Rev is short for Reverend, a parson's title

explanation.surface: A parson is held in a confined stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the clergyman's title inside the word for confined; 'stop' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening.

clue.text: Female body managing two silent minutes left off

indicators.note: managing suggests handling and rearranging, so the fodder letters are reordered
off says the letter for left is taken away from the word silent

explanation.surface: A women's organisation copes with two minutes of silence while someone left early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left off' removes L from SILENT, giving SIENT; then 'managing' rearranges TWO + SIENT + MINUTES. The Women's Institute is a British countrywide women's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Institute is a well-known British organisation of women, so a body of females.

clue.text: Future seed of Christmas, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks whether the phrase is being spoken, pointing to a sound-alike

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas, so of Christmas is of Yule

explanation.surface: Asking whether a seed for the future belongs to Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'of Yule' sounds like the botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the plant structure that develops into a seed after fertilisation, hence a future seed.

clue.text: Good little boy wearing English fur

indicators.note: wearing means the fur goes around the little boy, who is inside it

parts.note: sable is the prized fur of a small mammal
Tim is a short name for a boy, as in Tiny Tim

explanation.surface: A good little boy is dressed in English fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means the fur goes round the boy, as clothing goes round its wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means worthy of esteem, so good or admirable in character.

clue.text: In sport, to get plates of gold with silver backing one must pull out all the stops

definitions.text: one must pull out all the stops

indicators.note: In says the following letters sit inside the word for sport

parts.note: fun, as in making sport of someone or just for fun
L-plates are the learner plates fixed front and back on a British learner driver's car, giving two Ls
or is heraldic gold

indicators.note: backing means the chemical symbol for silver is read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A sporting winner is presented with gold plates on silver and must go all out to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates show a British car's driver is a learner; a car carries two. 'backing' turns the silver symbol round, and 'In' sets everything inside the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Full organ is the organist's term for playing with every stop drawn, so it is what you get when all stops are pulled out.

clue.text: Thanks to rank, archemperor with no son is included

indicators.note: is included means the trimmed emperor goes inside the word for rank

parts.note: grade means rank

indicators.note: with no means the letter for son is taken away

parts.note: Titus is the Roman emperor commemorated by the Arch of Titus in Rome

explanation.surface: Gratitude for promotion when an emperor without his son is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'archemperor' is a made-up word: the emperor with the Roman arch. 'with no son' drops his S, and 'is included' puts what remains inside the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is the feeling of thankfulness, expressed as thanks.

clue.text: Right oven for joint?

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Asking whether this right oven suits the Sunday joint.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, familiar in Kent as an oast house. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a roast is a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a cooked joint of meat, so the question mark signals an example of a joint.

clue.text: Consequence of jury's disagreement about point opposed to job for dog?

indicators.note: about means the phrase for a second trial goes around the other letters

parts.note: a hung jury leads to a retrial
E, east, is a compass point
v, versus, means opposed to

explanation.surface: A jury divided over a point argues about a dog's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E + V inside RETRIAL. A retriever dog fetches shot game.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval, fetching shot game, is the work of a gundog such as a retriever.

clue.text: Piece of music as teaching for class

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of music used for teaching a class.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'music' and continues through 'as' into 'teaching'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a rigid social class, as in the traditional Hindu social order.

clue.text: Volunteers to split churches, a monstrous order

indicators.note: to split means the volunteers go between the two church abbreviations

parts.note: CE, Church of England, twice for churches
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers split churches, an order that seems monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; CE is the Church of England. 'monstrous' alludes to sea monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetacea is the biological order of whales, which are huge animals of the kind called sea monsters.

clue.text: Champion's getting a job at police centre

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: centre means the inner letters of the word police, losing its ends

explanation.surface: A champion lands a job at the police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes the middle of POLICE, OLIC. An apostle can be any leading champion of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a zealous advocate of a cause, so apostolic describes what belongs to such a champion.

clue.text: Treating cancer I find horribly fascinating

indicators.note: treating suggests working on the letters and reshaping them

explanation.surface: Someone treating cancer finds it horribly fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treating' rearranges CANCER + I. Circe was the enchantress who turned Odysseus's men into pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe the enchantress bewitched men dangerously, so Circean means alluring but harmful.

clue.text: Tester about to have caught announcer

indicators.note: about means the tester's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a trier is one who tries or tests
to own is to have
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone testing things is about to have caught an announcer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the tester's word goes round the rest; the surface's 'about to' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who announced public news in the streets.

clue.text: Money heard to be of vantage

definitions.note: the definition completes the phrase coign of vantage, a noun

indicators.note: heard says a word is spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a coin is money

explanation.surface: Money is heard to be advantageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coign of vantage', from Shakespeare's Macbeth, is a corner with a good viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Coign survives in the phrase 'coign of vantage', meaning a projecting corner offering a good view.

clue.text: Drinking song?

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for everyone at once
a song where voices enter in turn with the same tune

explanation.definitionFit: A round is both a set of drinks for a group and a canon sung by voices entering in turn.

clue.text: Man of battle takes part of printer

indicators.note: takes here means takes away, so one part is removed from the battle name

parts.note: Inkerman was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier in battle gets hold of part of a printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of battle' reads as a soldier, but it is the MAN in INKERMAN, which 'takes' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inker is the component of a printing machine that applies ink.

clue.text: A lot of hot food, possibly cumulative, to resume with accents

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: curry, also spelt currie in older dictionaries, is spicy hot food

indicators.note: possibly says the following word's letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of hot food might pile up, leading someone to start again with accents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' takes CURRI from the old spelling CURRIE, and 'possibly' rearranges CUMULATIVE into CULUMVITAE.
explanation.definitionFit: A curriculum vitae is a CV, the document Americans call a résumé, spelt with its French accents.

clue.text: Leo, non-starter once, becomes allegedly aphrodisiac

parts.note: Leo Abse was a Welsh Labour MP famous for reform campaigns

indicators.note: non-starter means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A lion that was once a non-starter turns into an aphrodisiac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like the lion or star sign, but it is Leo Abse, a British MP. 'non-starter' drops the O of ONCE, leaving NCE. The proverb says absence makes the heart grow fonder.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder' claims being apart stirs love, so it is reputedly an aphrodisiac.

clue.text: Toy flipper said to belong to 15 down

definitions.note: the definition is read as one creature belonging to the order Cetacea, a noun phrase

indicators.note: said signals the toy flipper phrase is spoken to give the answer by sound

parts.note: a doll is a toy and a fin is a flipper

explanation.surface: A toy's flipper is said to belong to a whale order.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 down is CETACEA, the order of whales and dolphins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are toothed whales, members of the mammal order Cetacea.
